subject.title: Follow-up: optimize fallback order + add model-input config guardrail

question: Which fallback-ranking policy and model-input capability authority should OpenClaw enforce for configured provider models?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing runtime fallback ranking or rejecting configured modalities affects provider behavior and existing custom configs, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Document cost-first fallback policy and scope guardrail in #50287
options.body: Keep explicit configured fallback order unless a maintainer-approved benchmark says otherwise, and implement capability-aware validation in the focused guardrail tracker.

options.title: Enforce strict catalog authority now
options.body: Reject configured modalities that exceed bundled catalog metadata, accepting that existing custom multimodal provider configs may need migration or an explicit override.

options.title: Keep runtime behavior and add diagnostics only
options.body: Preserve all current configured modalities and ordering while improving warnings/docs so operators can repair bad metadata manually.

recommendation.title: Document cost-first fallback policy and scope guardrail in #50287
recommendation.body: Keep explicit configured fallback order unless a maintainer-approved benchmark says otherwise, and implement capability-aware validation in the focused guardrail tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: They are already carrying adjacent config/command hardening in #83391 and appear repeatedly in recent config and fallback history.
